stories.title: Pakistan Army Destroys Afghan Taliban Posts in Retaliatory Strikes
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Army destroyed several Afghan Taliban posts and military installations in border regions near South Waziristan and Parachinar. Security sources stated that the retaliatory strikes followed unprovoked firing by Kabul regime personnel in Angoor Adda, which caused civilian casualties.

During the operation, Afghan Taliban personnel reportedly abandoned their posts and fled amid multiple casualties. The recent clashes follow an earlier border incident where a civilian was killed and five family members were injured by a mortar shell, prompting Islamabad to demand that Kabul prevent militants from utilizing Afghan territory for attacks.

stories.title: Pakistan and Singapore Discuss Direct Flights and Bilateral Cooperation
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Singapore have explored the potential resumption of direct flights to improve business travel and people-to-people connections. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar held discussions with Singaporean Foreign Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan during an official visit marking 60 years of diplomatic relations.

The two officials agreed to boost bilateral trade, encourage business-to-business engagement, and expand collaboration in education, digital technologies, artificial intelligence, and climate domains. Furthermore, they reviewed regional developments, emphasizing dialogue for resolving disputes and reaffirming support for an independent Palestinian state based on pre-June 1967 borders.

stories.title: Geo News and UN Women Pakistan Sign Global Media Compact
stories.summary:
UN Women Pakistan and Geo News have partnered through the UN Women Global Media Compact to promote gender equality and women's empowerment. The alliance encourages media outlets to incorporate gender-responsive journalism and inclusive editorial practices into their daily operations.

The collaboration aims to challenge harmful stereotypes, eliminate discrimination, and amplify the voices and leadership of women and girls. Executives from both organizations emphasized that fair representation in news coverage is essential for shaping an equitable, informed society and shifting public perceptions of women across various professional fields.

stories.title: Pakistan Army Destroys Afghan Taliban Posts Following Border Firing
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Army targeted and destroyed several Afghan Taliban military positions near South Waziristan and Parachinar. State media reported that the military responded to unprovoked cross-border firing by Afghan forces in the Angoor Adda area, which resulted in one death and five injuries among local residents.

Using heavy weaponry, the retaliatory operation forced Afghan personnel to abandon their posts and flee, with reports indicating several casualties among the Taliban regime personnel. The exchange follows ongoing border tensions and Pakistani appeals for Kabul to address terrorist sanctuaries operating from Afghan territory.

stories.title: ایران، امریکہ تعلقات اور خطے کی صورتحال پر تبادلہ خیال کے لیے قطری وفد تہران پہنچ گیا
stories.summary:
ایرانی خبر رساں ایجنسی ارنا کے مطابق، قطری وزیرِ اعظم اور وزیرِ خارجہ کے سینئر مشیر کی قیادت میں ایک وفد جمعہ کی صبح تہران پہنچا۔ اس دورے کا مقصد دونوں ممالک کے درمیان تعلقات اور خطے کی تازہ ترین صورتحال پر مشاورت کرنا ہے۔ یہ سفارتی سرگرمی ایسے وقت میں سامنے آئی ہے جب علاقائی کشیدگی میں اضافہ دیکھا جا رہا ہے۔

اسی دوران، آبنائے ہرمز میں آئل ٹینکرز کو پیش آنے والے حادثات اور سکیورٹی خدات پر بھی رپورٹس سامنے آئی ہیں۔ دوسری جانب اتراکھنڈ کے ضلع چمولی میں بدری ناتھ سے دہرادون جانے والا ایک ہیلی کاپٹر لاپتا ہونے کے بعد حادثے کا شکار ہو گیا، جس میں عملے سمیت چھ افراد سوار تھے۔ مقامی انتظامیہ اور امدادی ٹیمیں متاثرہ علاقے میں ریسکیو آپریشن میں مصروف ہیں۔

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Closes Lower as KSE-100 Dips
stories.summary:
Trading at the Pakistan Stock Exchange ended in negative territory on Friday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index dropping significantly. The index fell by 784.19 points, representing a 0.47 percent decrease, to finish the session at 166,409.25 points compared to the previous close of 167,193.44 points.

Throughout the trading day, the market fluctuated between an intraday high of 167,338.73 and a low of 166,326.70. Regular market trading volume increased to over 825 million shares, while total traded value and overall market capitalization both declined relative to the preceding session.

stories.title: PSL Franchises Permitted Seven Retentions Ahead of Auction
stories.summary:
Pakistan Super League franchises can retain up to seven players for the tournament's 12th edition, provided they release a top-tier player from the previous auction into the general pool if they use the maximum limit. The regulations were unanimously approved by all eight franchises during a workshop in Islamabad.

The upcoming player auction will operate under a base salary cap of Rs45 crore, which can increase for teams utilizing direct signings or specific retentions. The retention deadline is scheduled for January 13 to allow franchises to evaluate player performances from ongoing domestic T20 competitions.

stories.title: Federal Constitutional Court Warns Against Ignoring Supreme Court Verdicts
stories.summary:
The Federal Constitutional Court cautioned that failing to implement Supreme Court verdicts undermines the legal system's foundation and democratic governance. The remarks were issued during a hearing on contempt petitions regarding the non-implementation of a December 2021 Supreme Court judgment concerning sacked government employees.

Justice Ali Baqar Najafi emphasized that judicial decisions represent legal mandates rather than mere recommendations, and compliance is essential for maintaining public trust. The underlying case involves laws affecting thousands of government workers whose employment status was impacted by previous rulings regarding the Sacked Employees Ordinance.

stories.title: PML-N Criticizes PTI Over Unfulfilled Promises and Alleged Corruption in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary:
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz leader Ikhtiar Wali Khan recently condemned the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, asserting that the party has failed to deliver meaningful progress in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa over the past thirteen years. Speaking at a gathering, he questioned the existence of any welfare state indicators and accused PTI figures of accumulating massive personal wealth under the banner of political change.

Wali highlighted unfulfilled pledges regarding millions of housing units and jobs, while alleging that several individuals associated with the PTI experienced exponential financial growth. He contrasted past financial standings with current multi-billion rupee assets allegedly held by local figures, questioning the authenticity of the promised revolution and reforms in the province.

stories.title: PTI Lawmakers Urge Opposition Leader Achakzai to Form Crucial Steering Committee Immediately
stories.summary:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf lawmakers have strongly urged National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai to promptly implement previous parliamentary party decisions by establishing a steering committee. During recent discussions, legislators expressed frustration over perceived delays, emphasizing that founding leader Imran Khan, his wife, and his sisters remain incarcerated and require urgent attention.

Tensions rose as Achakzai suggested waiting a few months, prompting lawmakers to question his urgency and reference potential alternative negotiation leads. The exchange follows broader internal debates regarding party direction, interactions with government figures, and the handling of advocacy efforts for detained leadership members.

stories.title: United Arab Emirates Equity Markets Drop Amid Disappointing Earnings and Regional Tensions
stories.summary:
Stock markets across the United Arab Emirates fell as soft corporate earnings and escalating regional security concerns weighed heavily on investor confidence. Major indices in Dubai and Abu Dhabi experienced declines, dragged down by losses in prominent financial institutions, developers, and sector operators reporting lower quarterly net profits.

Simultaneously, broader geopolitical anxieties intensified following reports of attacks on energy infrastructure and maritime vessels in the region, alongside discussions regarding military options. These regional developments contributed to a significant surge in global oil prices as traders braced for potential conflicts.

stories.title: Financial Sector Equities Push Sri Lankan Stock Market Lower in Quiet Trading Session
stories.summary:
Sri Lankan equity markets closed downward as selling pressure centered heavily on financial sector stocks. The CSE All-Share index finished lower, with prominent institutions such as Hatton National Bank PLC and LOLC Holdings PLC recording notable share price declines during the session.

Market activity slowed significantly compared to the previous session, reflected by lower overall trading volumes and reduced equity turnover figures. Exchange statistics indicated that domestic participants acted as net buyers, whereas foreign investors registered as net sellers of local equities.

stories.title: Iran Reports Detention of Two Oil Tankers and Destruction of US Unmanned Vessel
stories.summary:
The Revolutionary Guards Navy of Iran announced that two oil vessels were intercepted and halted in waters situated south of the Strait of Hormuz. Authorities stated that the tankers disregarded multiple radio warnings and attempted navigation through an unapproved channel within the strategic maritime route.

Additionally, Iranian officials reported the destruction of an unmanned United States vessel located within the eastern portion of the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of the announcement, military authorities from the United States had not provided immediate confirmation of the incidents.

stories.title: Federal Board of Revenue Clarifies Faceless Customs Assessment Is a Digital Modernization Step
stories.summary:
The Federal Board of Revenue has strongly defended its implementation of Faceless Customs Assessment, emphasizing that moving the Central Appraising Unit to Islamabad is a permanent digital upgrade designed to reduce official discretion. The tax authority noted that physical inspections and port operations will remain stationed in Karachi, allowing traders to resolve local grievances through designated collectorates.

Addressing industry concerns regarding clearance timelines and valuation disputes, the FBR reported substantial improvements in processing speeds and reiterated adherence to established legal valuation frameworks. The broader technological initiative aims to enhance transparency, minimize human interaction, and curb economic evasion through integrated digital documentation systems.

stories.title: Japan Begins First Clinical Stem-Cell Treatment for Parkinson's Disease
stories.summary:
A patient in Japan has become the first person in the world to undergo pioneering stem-cell therapy for Parkinson's disease. Sumitomo Pharma announced that the groundbreaking procedure took place at Kyoto University Hospital following regulatory approval earlier this year.

The treatment involves transplanting millions of induced pluripotent stem cells into the patient's brain to replace lost dopamine-producing cells. Parkinson's is a chronic neurological disorder affecting over 10 million people globally, causing motor difficulties. This milestone offers hope for addressing disease progression as the company monitors safety and plans further trials.

stories.title: Punjab Government Launches Free Training Course for Women
stories.summary:
The Punjab government has announced a free three-month Guest Relations Officer training course aimed at women under the Women Development Department’s SEHR Programme. Eligible female candidates aged 18 to 45 can apply for the practical training, which will take place at Lahore's Institute of Tourism and Hospitality Management.

The initiative is designed to equip women with essential hospitality skills and prepare them for future employment opportunities. With limited seats available, the department has encouraged interested applicants to contact authorities quickly to secure enrolment and take advantage of this free educational opportunity.

stories.title: بائنانس پر تاریخ کا بڑا سائبر حملہ، 6.3 ارب ڈالر کے ڈیجیٹل اثاثے متاثر
stories.summary:
دنیا کی معروف کرپٹو کرنسی کمپنی بائنانس کو ایک بڑے سائبر حملے کا سامنا کرنا پڑا ہے جس میں 6.3 ارب ڈالر مالیت کے ڈیجیٹل اثاثے متاثر ہوئے ہیں۔ کمپنی کا کہنا ہے کہ متاثرہ اثاثوں میں سے تقریبا نصف کو دیگر پلیٹ فارمز کی مدد سے منجمد کر دیا گیا ہے اور تمام نقصانات کا ازالہ کیا جائے گا۔ ابتدائی تحقیقات کے مطابق یہ ہیکنگ ممکنہ طور پر کمپنی کے ایک انجینئر کے لیپ ٹاپ کے ذریعے ہوئی۔

ماہر تجزیاتی اداروں اور کمپنیوں نے اس حملے کا تعلق شمالی کوریا کے ہیکنگ گروپ سے جوڑا ہے۔ بائنانس نے اس معاملے پر قانونی نافذ کرنے والے اداروں کے ساتھ تعاون کرنے کا عزم ظاہر کیا ہے جبکہ امریکی صارفین کا پلیٹ فارم اس سکیورٹی واقعے سے محفوظ رہا ہے۔ اس نوعیت کی بڑی چوریوں سے کرپٹو انڈسٹری کی سکیورٹی پر اہم سوالات اٹھ کھڑے ہوئے ہیں۔

stories.title: Zee Entertainment Reports Lower Profit Due to FIFA Broadcasting Costs
stories.summary:
India's Zee Entertainment Enterprises experienced a 38 percent drop in its quarterly profit for the July-September period. The decline was primarily driven by expenses related to the FIFA World Cup broadcast, expanded content offerings, and other strategic initiatives that offset subscription growth gains.

The broadcaster's consolidated profit fell to 478 million rupees, while overall expenses rose by 16 percent, lowering core profit margins to 3.2 percent. Although advertising revenue remained flat, subscription revenue climbed by 30 percent as the company continues to navigate shifting digital viewing trends and diversify its platform investments.

stories.title: Copper Prices Decline Amid Concerns Over Artificial Intelligence Spending
stories.summary:
Copper prices fell in London, putting the metal on track for its first monthly loss since June. Market participants worried that heavy spending on artificial intelligence may not yield adequate returns, prompting a broader shift in investor risk appetite toward bonds.

Despite the monthly dip, persistent near-term tightness supported continued market backwardation and strong Chinese import demand. Meanwhile, supply constraints persisted following disruptions at underground operations in Mongolia's Oyu Tolgoi mine and reduced vehicle crossing availability at the border.

stories.title: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Agree to Expand Energy and Mineral Cooperation
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen strategic ties in oil storage, refinery upgrades, minerals, and liquefied petroleum gas procurement. Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh bin Tami Al-Baqami finalized the arrangement in Islamabad, alongside an immediate announcement of same-day visa processing for Pakistani citizens.

The partnership aims to boost Pakistan's energy security by establishing tax-neutral commercial oil reserves and a major refining complex in Hub. These facilities will offer Saudi Arabia flexible supply routes and help diversify maritime transit risks associated with major global shipping chokepoints.

stories.title: Pakistan Prime Minister Praises Singapore's Remarkable Economic Transformation
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised Singapore's economic transformation during a meeting with visiting Singaporean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan in Islamabad. The discussions marked six decades of diplomatic ties and focused on enhancing bilateral trade, investment, infrastructure, and digital cooperation between the two nations.

The visit coincides with talks held alongside Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar regarding the potential resumption of direct flights to facilitate business and people-to-people contacts. Balakrishnan's visit represents the first trip by a Singaporean foreign minister to Pakistan in more than twenty years.

stories.title: Four Dead in AJK Cylinder Blast
stories.summary:
An explosion caused by a gas cylinder at a residential property in Azad Jammu and Kashmir's Bagh district resulted in four fatalities, including two women and two children. Another teenager sustained injuries and received medical treatment at a nearby hospital.

Police authorities launched an inquiry to determine the exact circumstances of the accident while dismissing unverified claims circulating on social media. Meanwhile, a separate vehicle fire in Tharparkar caused by a gas cylinder claimed eight lives.

stories.title: Sazgar Opens New Vehicle Plant in Philippines
stories.summary:
Pakistani vehicle manufacturer Sazgar Engineering Works Limited launched a new production facility in Laguna province, marking its entry into the Southeast Asian market. The site aims to produce about 12,000 three-wheelers annually, featuring both electric and internal combustion models.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. praised the investment for supporting local manufacturing and cleaner transportation. The facility is expected to generate jobs and business opportunities for local suppliers while advancing the company's international expansion goals.

stories.title: Hackers Steal Record $6.3 Billion from Binance Exchange
stories.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance suffered a record $6.3 billion theft by hackers, an attack analysts attributed to North Korea. Binance paused withdrawals and promised to cover the losses using company funds and reserves, while stablecoin issuers managed to quickly freeze roughly half of the stolen funds.

stories.title: Security Forces Intercept Five Drones in Balochistan
stories.summary:
Pakistani security personnel successfully neutralized five drones targeting a military check-post in the Albat area of Balochistan's Kharan district. Officials stated that the unmanned aerial vehicles were shot down promptly, preventing any damage to property or loss of life.

The incident occurs amid heightened regional tensions and a notable increase in cross-border security challenges. Islamabad continues to press neighboring authorities to prevent militant factions from operating across mutual borders.

stories.title: West Indies Seize Control Against Bangladesh in Mirpur
stories.summary:
Captain Roston Chase dismantled Bangladesh's batting lineup, reducing the hosts to 79-6 by the end of the third day in the opening Test at Mirpur. Bangladesh held a slim lead of 106 runs when fading light halted play, with two substitute and backup batters at the crease.

Earlier in the match, off-spinner Nayeem Hasan claimed four wickets to restrict the visitors to 245 runs, giving Bangladesh a narrow 27-run first-innings advantage. West Indies bowlers quickly erased that deficit through aggressive bowling spells following rain interruptions.

stories.title: Tech Giants Meta, TikTok, and X Lose UK Safety Data Lawsuit
stories.summary:
Meta, TikTok, and X have lost a legal challenge in London's High Court against British media regulator Ofcom. The tech companies contested information notices issued in February that demanded detailed content moderation metrics under the 2023 Online Safety Act.

The regulatory demands require data on removed posts, restricted visibility, and user exposure to harmful content to protect children online. The companies argued the rules imposed unprecedented burdens, but the court dismissed their case, leaving firms facing potential fines of up to 10% of global turnover for serious breaches.

stories.title: Gold Prices Drop Significantly Across Markets in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan decreased significantly on Friday, following a downward trend in international markets. According to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the price of gold per tola fell by Rs5,100 to settle at Rs420,536.

Similarly, the price for 10 grams of gold dropped by Rs4,373 to reach Rs360,541. Internationally, gold declined by $51 to $3,980 per ounce, while local silver prices also decreased by Rs238, bringing the rate to Rs5,530 per tola.

stories.title: Pakistan Government Confirms Rupee Devaluation Drove Up Mega Project Costs
stories.summary:
During a National Assembly session, the government confirmed that the devaluation of the Pakistani rupee significantly increased prices for petroleum, construction materials, and mega dam projects. Cement prices surged by 204 percent, high-speed diesel rose to Rs 472 per liter, and steel prices climbed by 268 percent due to the currency depreciation.

Exchange rate fluctuations added hundreds of billions of rupees to major infrastructure initiatives. The estimated Planning Commission cost for the Diamer Bhasha Dam escalated by Rs 642 billion to reach Rs 1,121 billion, while the Dasu Hydropower Project experienced a 258 percent cost overrun.

stories.title: Glenn Phillips Hits Century as New Zealand Defeats India
stories.summary:
Glenn Phillips scored a brilliant 107 off 49 balls to help New Zealand achieve their highest T20 score in an 87-run victory over India in Auckland. Phillips hit 10 sixes and shared a rapid partnership with Michael Bracewell, who contributed 65 runs from 25 deliveries, propelling New Zealand to a record total of 259-7.

In response, India struggled against the New Zealand bowling attack, collapsing to 172-9. Jacob Duffy led the bowling figures with four wickets for 23 runs, while captain Mitchell Santner claimed two wickets, securing a commanding win ahead of the final series match in Hamilton.

stories.title: Pakistani Rupee Edges Up Slightly Against US Dollar
stories.summary:
The Pakistani rupee recorded a marginal gain against the US dollar in the inter-bank market, closing at 276.75 compared to the previous session's rate of 276.76. The slight uptick occurred as global markets tracked falling US Treasury yields and shifting currency trends.

Simultaneously, global oil prices advanced significantly, heading toward substantial monthly gains. Brent crude futures and US West Texas Intermediate rose due to ongoing supply risks highlighted by an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Sri Lanka Inflation Rises to 8.3% in October Due to Energy Costs
stories.summary:
Sri Lanka's Colombo Consumer Price Index increased by 8.3% year-on-year in October, rising from an 8% increase the previous month, according to the Statistics Department. Food inflation reached 8.8%, while the non-food category grew by 8%. Inflation has remained at a three-year high since July, driven by escalating energy costs resulting from the conflict involving Iran.

The Central Bank of Sri Lanka has established an inflation target of 5% and anticipates price pressures to decrease gradually after next March. Despite an unexpected 100 basis point rate hike in May, borrowing rates have been maintained at current levels as the nation prepares to unveil its 2027 budget on November 12.

stories.title: حب الوطنی کے سرٹیفکیٹ کی ضرورت نہیں، مولانا عبدالغفور حیدری
stories.summary:
جمعیت علماء اسلام کے سیکریٹری جنرل مولانا عبدالغفور حیدری نے پارلیمنٹ میں میڈیا سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ انہیں کسی سے حب الوطنی کا سرٹیفکیٹ لینے کی ضرورت نہیں ہے۔ انہوں نے مؤقف اختیار کیا کہ وزرا نے صرف الزام تراشی کی ہے لیکن وہ کچھ بھی ثابت نہیں کر سکے۔

مولانا عبدالغفور حیدری کا مزید کہنا تھا کہ ریاست ہم سب کی ہے اور ملک میں آئے روز قرضے بڑھ رہے ہیں جبکہ امن و امان کی صورتحال خراب ہو چکی ہے۔ انہوں نے یہ بھی کہا کہ خان آف قلات کو اغواء کیا گیا ہے اور ریاست کو چاہیے کہ انہیں واپس لائے۔

stories.title: Three Police Personnel Killed in Separate Attacks Across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary:
Three law enforcement personnel were killed in separate attacks across different districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Incidents in Bajaur, Lakki Marwat, and Bannu claimed the lives of a police constable, another constable, and a Counter-Terrorism Department official. During a subsequent pursuit operation in Lakki Marwat, security forces and local volunteers engaged in a firefight that resulted in the deaths of two suspected terrorists.

The violence follows a recent military operation in Dera Ismail Khan that left six militants and two soldiers dead. These security incidents highlight ongoing counter-terrorism operations in the region as authorities work to track down remaining suspects involved in the latest attacks.

stories.title: PSL Sets January 13 Deadline for Franchise Player Retention Lists
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Super League has announced January 13, 2027, as the final date for all eight franchises to submit their player retention lists ahead of the Season 12 Player Auction. The timeline was finalized during a workshop chaired by PSL CEO Salman Naseer at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, where team representatives approved updated tournament regulations and squad composition frameworks.

Under the new guidelines, each franchise can retain up to seven players and operate under a salary cap ranging from a minimum of PKR 36.5 crore to a maximum of PKR 50.5 crore. The upcoming player auction is scheduled for January 23, marking only the second such auction in the history of the T20 league.

stories.title: MIT Solutions Defeats SBP to Claim President’s Trophy Grade-I
stories.summary:
Markhor IT Solutions secured a 51-run victory over the State Bank of Pakistan at Bagh-e-Jinnah to capture the President’s Trophy Grade-I championship. Defending a target of 237, MIT Solutions dismissed SBP for 185 in the opening session of the final day, with Khalid Usman leading the bowling attack by taking four wickets for 38 runs.

SBP resumed their second innings at 165-7, but overnight batters were unable to mount a sustained resistance. Hasan Raza top-scored for SBP with a resilient 73 runs, but a late batting collapse sealed their defeat, handing the title to MIT Solutions following strong performances from Usman and Aamir Jamal.

stories.title: Binance Freezes Billions Following Complex Cryptocurrency Security Breach
stories.summary:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced it is addressing a complex security breach impacting approximately $6.3 billion in funds, with roughly half of that amount successfully frozen. While initial investigations pointed to a compromised employee laptop, subsequent reviews revealed multiple breach points. Blockchain investigators and platform executives reported that substantial assets were frozen in coordination with stablecoin issuers.

Industry analysts and blockchain firms have linked the attack to North Korea-associated hacker groups. In response to the incident, Binance temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while working alongside law enforcement agencies and industry partners to trace stolen assets and secure the platform.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Rises on Bargain Buying and Firm Edible Oils
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures closed over 1% higher, achieving their fourth monthly gain in five months, driven by bargain buying and stronger Dalian palm olein and Chicago soyoil prices. The benchmark January delivery contract on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange increased by 1.43% to settle at 4,682 ringgit per metric ton.

Market participants are awaiting Malaysia's upcoming October export and production data, alongside inventory reports scheduled for November 10. Additionally, rising crude oil prices and ongoing supply risks associated with geopolitical tensions provided technical support and enhanced the attractiveness of palm oil as a biodiesel feedstock.

stories.title: Association Opposes Foreign Pilot Recruitment in Pakistani Airlines
stories.summary: The Aircraft Owners and Operators Association has expressed its opposition to the employment of foreign pilots by Pakistani airlines.

stories.title: Karachi Hospitals Report Surge in Influenza Cases
stories.summary: Medical facilities in Karachi are experiencing a sharp increase in patient visits as the city is struck by a wave of flu cases.

stories.title: India Reports Fiscal Deficit at 42.1% of Target in September
stories.summary:
India's fiscal deficit reached 7.15 trillion rupees, or $75.24 billion, between April and September, marking 42.1% of the full-year target for the financial period ending in March. Government figures released on Friday show this compares to a deficit of 5.7 trillion rupees recorded during the same timeframe last year. Net tax receipts rose to 12.8 trillion rupees, while total government expenditures climbed to 25.5 trillion rupees, including 6.5 trillion rupees allocated for physical infrastructure capital spending. 

The central government aims to cap its annual fiscal deficit at 4.3% of the gross domestic product, equivalent to 16.96 trillion rupees. Meanwhile, non-tax revenue increased slightly to 4.8 trillion rupees, and the merchandise trade deficit for September widened to $30.21 billion. Monitoring these fiscal indicators is vital for understanding the nation's economic health and adherence to established budgetary boundaries as the fiscal year progresses.

stories.title: Netanyahu's Bloc Leads Israeli Election But Misses Majority Threshold
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing and far-right coalition secured 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, finishing ahead of the opposition but falling short of the 61-seat majority required to form a government. Final results released Friday by the Central Elections Committee showed the centrist opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot trailing with 48 seats, while Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List emerged as potential kingmakers with a combined 19 seats. The fragmented outcome paves the way for weeks of difficult coalition negotiations or the possibility of a fresh election if talks collapse. 

The vote tally followed unproven allegations from Netanyahu's camp that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding from Qatar to influence the election through vote-buying, specifically targeting Raam. Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu of incitement. Although domestic security service Shin Bet launched an investigation into suspected irregularities, election officials dismissed claims of widespread issues as baseless, as opposition figures accused the Prime Minister of attempting to delegitimize the results.

stories.title: Indian rupee records best monthly gain in eight months
stories.summary: The Indian rupee closed higher at 94.95 per dollar, achieving its strongest monthly gain since February. Policy interventions by the Reserve Bank of India, including capital inflow measures and steps to curb dollar demand from oil companies, supported the currency despite pressure from high oil prices and portfolio outflows.

stories.title: Indian shares snap losing streak with strong October gains
stories.summary: Indian stock indexes ended a two-month losing streak in October, driven by resilient earnings, IT sector growth, and tax-relief hopes. The Nifty 50 and Sensex rose 1.9% and 2.7% respectively for the month. IT shares surged 17.7%, led by major firms like Tata Consultancy Services and Infosys, despite gains being capped by rising crude prices.

stories.title: Pakistan reports weekly inflation drop of 0.35 percent
stories.summary: Official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics indicates that weekly short-term inflation dropped by 0.35 per cent.

stories.title: Pakistan Short-Term Inflation Rises to 11.32% on Food Prices
stories.summary:
Pakistan's short-term inflation climbed to 11.32% year-on-year for the week ending October 29, driven primarily by costlier perishable food items and persistent energy price increases. Official data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics showed that out of 51 monitored commodities, 15 increased in price, 12 declined, and 24 remained unchanged. Persistent rises in petroleum and diesel prices continued to fuel cost-push inflation, placing mounting financial pressure on households across the country.

The weekly Sensitive Price Index recorded notable price surges for items such as tomatoes, potatoes, diesel, and pulse gram, while electricity charges for the first quarter, chicken, and eggs saw declines. Tracking these weekly changes is essential for understanding short-term price fluctuations in essential consumer goods and services, helping policymakers and citizens gauge ongoing cost-of-living pressures in local markets.

stories.title: گائے ذبح کرنے کے مقدمے میں تین افراد کو عمر قید
stories.summary:
انڈین ریاست گجرات کے ضلع گاندھی نگر کی ایک عدالت نے گائے ذبح کرنے کے مقدمے میں تین افراد کو عمر قید اور تین لاکھ روپے جرمانے کی سزا سنا دی ہے۔ عدالت نے اس فیصلے میں گائے کی مذہبی اہمیت کو اجاگر کرتے ہوئے ہندو مذہبی کتب کا حوالہ بھی دیا۔

اضافی سیشن جج نے گجرات اینیمل پریزرویشن ایکٹ کے تحت ملزمان کو مزید دس سال قید اور جرمانے کی سزا بھی دی جو بیک وقت نافذ ہوگی۔ استغاثہ کے مطابق ملزمان کو مالی فائدے کے لیے گائے ذبح کرنے اور گوشت فروخت کرنے کے الزام میں پکڑا گیا تھا۔

stories.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio Hosts G20 Ministers in Atlanta
stories.summary:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta, Georgia, for discussions marked by strong divisions over ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and Iran, alongside surging global energy prices. The meeting, which includes Russia’s Sergei Lavrov, precedes a December leaders' summit in Miami and addresses geopolitical strains affecting economic security and vital supply chains. With Washington holding the rotating G20 presidency, the talks focus on energy access and freedom of navigation following trade route disruptions caused by Middle Eastern tensions.

The gathering is expected to yield a US-drafted chair summary rather than a formal consensus statement due to disagreements among member nations, particularly concerning free navigation in strategic waterways like the Strait of Hormuz. The Trump administration aims to steer the G20 back toward core economic growth and deregulation. The outcomes of these discussions will significantly influence the agenda of the upcoming Miami summit and international cooperation on pressing security and economic shocks.

stories.title: PPP Delegation Urges Senate Opposition to Join Electoral Reforms Committee
stories.summary:
A Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) delegation met with Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas on Friday to encourage opposition participation in a proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms. Senator Sherry Rehman stated that Abbas welcomed the initiative and agreed to consult before delivering a formal response. The proposal was initially introduced by PPP chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari in the National Assembly to address opposition concerns regarding electoral transparency and past allegations of vote rigging.

The outreach follows a similar meeting with National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai, as the PPP seeks to engage opposition lawmakers who previously boycotted parliamentary standing committees. Party leaders emphasized that committee participation is vital for strengthening the role of Parliament and allowing dissenting parties to voice reservations. Securing broader legislative engagement is considered crucial for fostering political consensus and advancing national governance reforms.

stories.title: لاہور: شہری پر جھوٹا مقدمہ درج کرنے والا سب انسپکٹر گرفتار
stories.summary:
لاہور میں چودہ ماہ قبل ایک شہری کے خلاف جھوٹا مقدمہ درج کر کے اسے گرفتار کرنے والے سب انسپکٹر امجد رضا کو انکوائری رپورٹ میں قصوروار ثابت ہونے پر حراست میں لے لیا گیا ہے۔

پنجاب پولیس کی رپورٹ کے مطابق ملزم سب انسپکٹر نے ایک دکان کے مالک سے ملی بھگت کر کے متاثرہ شہری زنیر کو اغواء کیا، اس پر تشدد کیا اور منشیات کا جھوٹا مقدمہ درج کیا۔ سی سی ٹی وی فوٹیجز اور دیگر شواہد سے یہ مقدمہ جھوٹا ثابت ہونے پر کارروائی عمل میں لائی گئی۔

stories.title: اسکردو: گھر سے میاں بیوی اور دو بچوں کی لاشیں برآمد
stories.summary:
گلگت بلتستان کے شہر اسکردو کی مدینہ کالونی میں ایک گھر سے ایک ہی خاندان کے چار افراد کی لاشیں ملی ہیں۔ پولیس حکام کے مطابق جاں بحق ہونے والوں میں میاں بیوی اور ان کے دو کمسن بچے شامل ہیں۔

پولیس کا کہنا ہے کہ چاروں افراد کو چھری اور کلہاڑی کے وار کر کے قتل کیا گیا ہے۔ بچوں کی عمریں ایک سے پانچ سال کے درمیان ہیں جبکہ لاشیں اسپتال منتقل کر کے واقعے کا مقدمہ درج کر لیا گیا ہے اور مزید تحقیقات جاری ہیں۔

stories.title: Pakistani Court Extends Remand of US Stamp Fraud Suspect
stories.summary:
A judicial magistrate in Lahore granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency a four-day physical remand extension for Faheem Akram, the prime suspect in a Rs35 billion online counterfeit US postage stamp fraud. Investigators presented Akram and co-suspect Naeem in court on Friday after their previous custody expired, aiming to continue interrogations regarding the illicit scheme. The website, active since August 2023, allegedly sold over five million counterfeit US postage labels, causing financial losses exceeding $126 million to the US Postal Service.

The investigation involves extensive digital and forensic techniques, including tracking financial transactions across 16 bank accounts linked to the suspect and his family members. US authorities previously indicted Akram in Florida, prompting international cooperation and web domain seizures. Local law enforcement agencies formed multiple special teams across Pakistan to map out the financial trails and determine the full operational scale of the fraudulent network.

stories.title: قصور: کھیر کھانے سے ایک ہی خاندان کے پانچ افراد جاں بحق
stories.summary:
صوبہ پنجاب کے ضلع قصور میں کھیر کھانے کے بعد ایک ہی خاندان کے پانچ افراد ہلاک ہو گئے۔ کنگن پور کے قریب واقع گاؤں کے اس خاندان نے 22 اکتوبر کو ناشتے میں کھیر کھائی تھی جس کے بعد ان کی طبیعت خراب ہو گئی۔

ابتداء میں خاندان نے مقامی روحانی معالج سے رابطہ کیا لیکن حالت بہتر نہ ہونے پر انہیں اسپتال منتقل کیا گیا۔ علاج کے دوران قصور اور پھر لاہور کے جنرل اسپتال میں تینوں بیٹے، والد اور آخر میں والدہ بھی جاں بحق ہو گئیں۔ پولیس نے نمونے فرانزک لیب بھجوا دیے ہیں۔

stories.title: نہرِ خیام پر کنکریٹ کی چھت کی منظوری نہیں لی گئی، منعم ظفر
stories.summary:
امیر جماعت اسلامی کراچی منعم ظفر نے سندھ ہائی کورٹ کے باہر میڈیا سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ نہرِ خیام پر کنکریٹ کی چھت ڈالنے کی منظوری سٹی کونسل سے نہیں لی گئی۔ انہوں نے مطالبہ کیا کہ اس کام کی تفصیلات عوام کے سامنے رکھی جائیں۔

ان کا کہنا تھا کہ پوری نہر کو چائنہ کٹنگ کے حوالے کیا جا رہا ہے اور سیوریج کا پانی سمندر میں جا رہا ہے۔ انہوں نے مزید بتایا کہ اس تعمیرات کے لیے سندھ انوائرنمنٹل پروٹیکشن ایجنسی سے بھی ماحولیاتی منظوری حاصل نہیں کی گئی۔
